evals.name: h100-ridge-point
evals.prompt: What's the roofline ridge point of an H100 SXM in bf16, and what does it tell me about attention?
evals.expected_output: 989 TFLOP/s dense (not the 1979 sparse figure) / 3.35 TB/s = ~295 FLOP/byte; attention's AI is about the head dim (64-128), well below it, so attention is memory-bound.

assertions.description: Uses the DENSE bf16 peak of ~989 TFLOP/s and notes NVIDIA's 1979 headline is with sparsity
Computes a ridge point of roughly 295 FLOP/byte from 989/3.35
States attention's arithmetic intensity is approximately the head dimension, 64–128
Gives the concrete naive-attention traffic figure — at b=1, a=32, s=8192 in bf16 the score tensor is about 4.3 GB per layer, written and read several times
Notes the ridge point ROSE from about 153 on A100-80GB to 295 on H100, so more kernels are memory-bound on newer hardware than on older
Notes the A100 40GB has a HIGHER ridge point (about 201) than the 80GB (about 153) because bandwidth differs at equal peak

evals.name: why-flashattention
evals.prompt: Why is FlashAttention faster than naive attention? Does it reduce the number of FLOPs?
evals.expected_output: No FLOP reduction; it is IO-aware — never materializes the s x s score matrix in HBM, using tiling plus online softmax, and recomputes scores in backward.

assertions.description: States explicitly that FLOPs are unchanged — it is a memory-traffic optimization, not a math one
Says it avoids writing the s×s score matrix to HBM by tiling and keeping blocks in shared memory
Names online softmax — maintaining a running max and running sum with a rescaling correction — as what makes tiling possible
Notes the backward pass recomputes the scores from Q, K, V and saved statistics rather than storing them
Quantifies the saving, e.g. that HBM traffic drops from O(s²) to O(s·d) or gives a concrete GB figure

evals.name: gpu-util-is-misleading
evals.prompt: nvidia-smi says GPU utilization is 100% but our training is clearly slow. Doesn't 100% mean we're compute-bound?
evals.expected_output: No. Utilization is the fraction of intervals with any kernel resident, not fraction of peak FLOPs. A memory-bound kernel reports 100%. Asks for achieved FLOP/s and DRAM throughput.

assertions.description: States that 100% utilization does not mean compute-bound
Defines nvidia-smi utilization as the fraction of sampled time with any kernel resident, not a fraction of peak FLOPs
Gives the concrete case that a memory-bound kernel saturating nothing still reports 100%
Names achieved FLOP/s and DRAM throughput (or MFU) as the metrics that actually place the kernel on the roofline

evals.name: fp32-master-weights
evals.prompt: 메모리를 아끼려고 fp32 master weight를 없애고 bf16만 쓰려는데 괜찮을까?
evals.expected_output: Not a memory optimization but a correctness change: bf16 has 8 significand bits so relative updates below ~2^-8 = 0.0039 round away; typical Adam updates are 1e-3 to 1e-6 relative. Mentions stochastic rounding as the escape.

assertions.description: Frames dropping the fp32 master as a correctness change, not a memory optimization
States bf16's ~8 significand bits give a smallest representable relative change of about 2⁻⁸ ≈ 0.004
Notes typical Adam updates are ~1e-3 to 1e-6 relative to the weight, i.e. below that threshold, so they round away
Warns the failure is silent — the run does not crash, it just stops learning
Mentions stochastic rounding (or Kahan summation) as the way to actually make this work

evals.name: fp8-doubles-ridge
evals.prompt: If I switch from bf16 to fp8 on H100, do I automatically get a 2x speedup?
evals.expected_output: No. FP8 doubles peak FLOP/s but not bandwidth, so the ridge point doubles from ~295 to ~591; ops that were marginally compute-bound become memory-bound and gain far less than 2x.

assertions.description: Says the speedup is not automatically 2x
States the ridge point doubles because peak FLOP/s doubles while HBM bandwidth is unchanged
Gives the fp8 ridge point as roughly 591 FLOP/byte versus about 295 for bf16
Notes fp8 needs per-tensor scaling factors due to its tiny dynamic range, and/or that e4m3 is used for forward and e5m2 for gradients

evals.name: vocab-tile-padding
evals.prompt: 누가 vocab size를 50257에서 50304로 바꾸면 학습이 빨라진다고 하는데, 진짜야? 왜?
evals.expected_output: Yes: tensor-core GEMMs run in fixed tiles, so a dimension not a multiple of 64/128 wastes the final tile. 50304 is the next multiple of 64. Extends to h, FFN size, and per-rank shards h/t.

assertions.description: Confirms the claim is real
Explains that tensor-core GEMMs execute in fixed tiles, so a partially-filled final tile costs as much as a full one
Notes 50304 is the next multiple of 64 (and 128) above 50257
Generalizes the check to other GEMM dimensions such as hidden size, FFN intermediate size, or the per-rank shard h/t after tensor parallelism
